What Children Really Notice About Honesty

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Recent findings suggest that as parents, most of us want to raise honest children.
  • Recent findings suggest that but there is another way children learn about honesty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Recent findings suggest that as parents, most of us want to raise honest children. We tell them honesty is important. We remind them to tell the truth when they make mistakes or do something wrong. We praise their honesty when they admit wrongdoing. And we explain why lying can damage trust.

Recent findings suggest that but there is another way children learn about honesty. They are not only listening to what we say. They are also watching what we do.

And sometimes those two things do not match.

Perhaps we tell our child that honesty is notable but then claim they are younger than they really are to get a discounted movie ticket. Or we remind our child to take responsibility when they make mistakes, yet avoid taking responsibility for our own. Most of us can think of situations where our actions do not perfectly align with the messages we are trying to teach.

What do children make of these mixed messages?

Industry observers note that my colleagues and I recently conducted a study to explore this question. We wanted to understand how children think about honesty when parents' actions either support or contradict the lessons they teach.

Sources indicate that we recruited 127 children between 5 and 12 years of age. The children listened to stories about parents and their children. In some stories, the parent stressed the importance of honesty and then behaved honestly. In others, the parent promoted honesty but later engaged in dishonest behaviour. After each story, the children were asked what they thought about the parent and what lessons another child might learn from observing that parent.

One finding stood out: children noticed when parents' words and actions did not match. Parents who practised what they preached were viewed more positively than parents whose behaviour contradicted their message.

Even more interesting, when children's predictions depended on choosing between a parent's words and a parent's actions, they often gave greater weight to the parent's behaviour. In other words, when there was a conflict between what a parent said and what a parent did, children frequently treated the behaviour as the more important source of information.

In a recent development, children also viewed truthful parents as more trustworthy than parents who lied. Whether the lie was told to avoid hurting someone's feelings or to avoid getting into trouble mattered less than one might expect. The simple fact that the parent chose honesty influenced children's judgments. In short, children preferred parents whose actions matched the values they claimed to hold.

Industry observers note that our findings suggest that children are not simply listening to what parent say, they are also paying attention to what parents do. When parents’ actions are consistent with their messages about honesty, children receive a clear message about the value of truthfulness. When words and actions conflict, that message becomes more ambiguous.

Recent findings suggest that this does not mean parents must be perfect. Perfection is neither realistic nor necessary. However, parents should remember that everyday behaviour teaches powerful lessons. Children learn about honesty not only from conversations, but also from watching how adults handle mistakes, promises, responsibilities, and everyday challenges.

The findings suggest several practical ways parents can promote honesty.

Industry observers note that parents often believe that the key to teaching honesty is telling children that honesty matters. That message is certainly vital. But our research suggests that children are paying just as much attention to something else: whether we live by the values we teach.

When it comes to honesty, children appear to be asking not only, "What did my parent say?" but also, "What did my parent do?".

Bélanger, E., Crossman, A. M., & Talwar, V. (2026). Practice what you preach? Children’s evaluations of parents’ verbal messages and social modeling of honesty and lie-telling. Journal of Experimental Child Psychology, 268, 106528. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022096526000809.

Max Verstappen and George Russell start side by side on the front row for the Las Vegas Grand Prix Saturday evening, thanks to a five-place grid penalty for pole-sitter and world champion Kimi Antonelli.

With this front row, there is no love lost over their careers and, more specifically, this weekend, as Russell enters the race upset, with a first step in following the clash between the two and FP3, in which Russell rebounded to top the time charts with a time of 1:34.805.

Industry observers note that in FP3, Verstappen passed Russell and, in the next corner, braked hard, forcing the Mercedes driver to run off the racing line and towards the barrier in an evasive maneuver. Following the brake, the two banged wheels in a session without consequence. After the light collision, Verstappen flipped off Russell on the next straight. The drivers were called in front of the stewards, and Verstappen was given a warning after being found to have made an “unpredictable change of direction under braking.”.

Industry observers note that this was the third time during FP3 that Verstappen pulled such a move, as he was already under investigation for doing the same to the Alpine of Franco Colapinto and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Russell’s woes with Verstappen’s move this week is that he finds that the four-time champion has a pattern of behavior that screws over those he’s competing against. In this case overtaking at the start of a practice lap.

With FP3 being the only dry practice sessions of the weekend, emotions were elevated as drivers were pressed to figure out how the new car works on the coldest street circuit of the year.

“There’s nothing in the rules that claims you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but you’re screwing this person over,” Russell said post race to sky sports Italia. “He does this week in and week out with many drivers and everyone accepts it.

“I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to this guy.”.

When the comments were shared with Verstappen, he brushed them off, saying he wasn’t going to waste his time on the comments before adding that in racing there are no gentleman’s agreements.

“I've never heard of a gentleman’s agreement in my life, Verstappen said.

Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports that, with his driver and his Red Bull advisory on the front row, we should expect cinema if they go for the same line into the opening corner of the Grand Prix tonight.

“If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching,” Wolff mentioned.

This is the first time this year that the two start next to each other on the front row and the ninth across their careers.

The Secrets to Whole-Life Training

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1365 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • Industry observers note that there’s more to getting fit than chasing a PR or sweating through another bootcamp class.
  • Recent findings suggest that the key is making different types of exercise work together, rather than relying on any one activity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that there’s more to getting fit than chasing a PR or sweating through another bootcamp class. The real payoff? Being ready for the next workout, the weekend adventure, the everyday hustle, and all the years ahead.

Recent findings suggest that the key is making different types of exercise work together, rather than relying on any one activity. This multifaceted and well-rounded approach to training means you’re working more than the muscles, because you’re focused on the movements.

When you approach training this way, you’re literally starting from the ground up. “Every single step you take, your foot is the first thing that hits the ground,” indicates Jen Perez, DC, a chiropractic physician who combines clinical practice and education to help people improve foot health and lower-body function. “It’s the first thing that interfaces with the world around you, what has to be strong and springy when you want to run or jump or dance or ski.”.

A whole-life, well-rounded training plan comes down to five essentials, according to Courtney Conley, DC, a best-selling author and chiropractic physician with more than two decades of clinical experience:.

Recent findings suggest that cardio and strength may already be part of your routine, but the others can be easier to overlook; especially because they deliver numerous movement benefits that you may not equate them with. For example, Conley emphasizes that power training isn’t just for athletes; it also has practical life applications. “Getting up and out of your chair, having good reaction time, and making sure you don’t fall if you step off a curb and trip are all part of that category,” she says.

Recent findings suggest that mobility means moving freely through a full range of motion, while balance helps you adjust to changing surfaces and react when your footing shifts—it isn’t just holding a tree pose. “There are thousands of nerve endings in each foot that help communicate to our brain where we are in space,” Perez explains. That feedback, combined with the feet’s ability to grip the ground, helps keep you steady.

Recovery is what allows your body to benefit from hard training, yet Conley says it’s often ignored: “I think one of the biggest mistakes is that people don’t recover.” Sleep, adequate nutrition, and lighter days that deliberately scale back workout volume or intensity give your body time to adapt and help you come back ready for your next workout.

Industry observers note that the work you do in the gym should go beyond just trying to look good and prepare you for the demands of everyday movement. For strength and power work, Conley recommends deadlifts and kettlebell swings to train the hip-hinge pattern, along with farmer’s carries to build strength in the core and lower body. “I love all that functional movement,” she claims. “A sled push is also great, because as your heel comes off the ground, you’re hitting all the intrinsic muscles of your foot.”.

In a recent development, certain machine exercises may not seem so functional but can address specific weaknesses. For instance, Conley states she often uses seated calf raises to strengthen the tissues around the Achilles and leg extensions to isolate the quadriceps. She also recommends plyometrics—quick, explosive jumping and hopping drills—to develop power. “Try double-leg and single-leg hops, forward and backward, side to side, and zigzag moves,” she says, recommending five or six sets of 10 reps per exercise for plyometric movements.

Industry observers note that ankle and massive-toe mobility are number one on Conley’s priority list for things you should focus on outside of your regular workouts. “When you can’t propel through the ankle, you’re going to get there by extending the knee so you can push yourself forward,” she indicates. “People come in with knee or back pain when oftentimes it’s an ankle problem.” She suggests making mobility a regular part of the week rather than waiting until something feels stiff or restricted. Even a short dedicated session can help you maintain the range of motion your training requires.

Recent findings suggest that perez indicates your feet also adapt to the surface beneath you and absorb force. “If you think of your foot like a trampoline, every single step we take, whether walking or running, the foot needs to be able to lower, which is that mobility piece, then it needs to be able to spring back up.”.

Perez recommends two simple drills to improve foot mobility and strength: the Foot Handshake, where you weave the fingers of one hand between the toes of the opposite foot and gently circle the foot at the ankle; and Lift, Spread, and Reach, where you lift all five toes, spread them apart, then reach them forward as you lower them.

Another way you can activate your feet during training is to choose your shoes wisely. When it comes to footwear, Perez has one non-negotiable regardless of the activity: a wide toe box that lets your toes spread naturally. “If your toes are more narrow than the ball of your foot, that tells me we’ve got some work to do,” she indicates. In practice, that can mean adding foot mobility and strength drills to your routine and choosing shoes that let your toes spread naturally.

Recent findings suggest that perez favors Altra Fit, both for her own footwear and when recommending shoes to others, because it gives the forefoot more room than a traditionally tapered toe box. Conley’s experience demonstrates how the amount of cushioning that feels right can change over time as your foot gets stronger and needs more targeted footwear. She started out in the Altra FWD VIA 2, a cushioned shoe with the original (read: roomiest) FootShape™ and a 4 mm drop that felt familiar coming from conventional running shoes. “I was getting some toe splay and my foot was getting stronger,” she recalls. “Now I put them on, and it’s too much shoe for me because I don’t need as much cushioning.”.

Industry observers note that that’s where having options comes in. Altra’s Torin 9 offers a more moderate level of cushioning, standard footshape (secure midfoot), and a zero-drop platform that is good for running and still takes advantage of the Altra Fit that helps your feet get stronger as you log miles. For a lower-profile option, the Altra Escalante 5 has low cushioning, a 24 mm stack height, zero drop, and the original, roomiest FootShape fit.

In a recent development, “You’ll want to use the least amount of shoe assistance necessary for the activity,” Perez recommends. A lower-profile, more flexible shoe, like the Escalante 5, offers more ground feel for strength training, while extra cushioning or rocker geometry, found in the Torin 9 and FWD VIA 2, may be useful on longer runs. Conley agrees that a plush running shoe isn’t necessarily the best tool for lifting. “You can’t feel the ground,” she indicates of maximalist shoes. “You’re standing on something that decreases your sensory acuity.”.

If multidimensional fitness is upcoming to you, Conley recommends starting with manageable strength work (two or three days a week), walking, and one or two mobility or foot exercises, and build gradually as your strength and capacity improve. “Do things that challenge you, but not to the point where you start to feel overwhelmed,” she says.

If you already work out or run regularly, consider what’s missing from your routine while prioritizing your main goal. Conley suggests making room for mobility, balance, and power work, and fitting short foot-strength and mobility exercises into existing workouts. Do it while you’re fresh, adjusting your workload when running volume increases or recovery suffers.

According to recent reports, the goal isn’t to do everything all the time or become an expert at every type of training. It’s to build a body that can keep doing the things you love. Run the trails. Lift the heavy stuff. Hike the mountain. Get down on the floor with your kids and grandkids—and have the strength and mobility to get back up again.

Inside, the latest Han adopts BYD’s updated interior design. The new setup includes a floating center infotainment screen and a digital instrument panel behind a three-spoke steering wheel.

The center console is also updated with two wireless phone chargers and cupholders without covers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.

In a recent development, ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron. You need iron in order to make healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Iron is also important for bone marrow, organs, healthy muscles, and brain development.

As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, consumers are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.

Recent findings suggest that customers have also shared images of their face before and after taking iron supplements or getting an iron infusion. Videos about “ferritin face” have garnered millions of views on various platforms.

However, medical professionals state that your appearance alone is not enough to diagnose iron deficiency.

In a recent development, “It’s vital to understand that ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis, nor is it a confirmed symptom of iron deficiency. While some people with iron deficiency can appear pale due to low hemoglobin levels in their red blood cells, there are many other symptoms to consider,” noted Daniel Atkinson, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and clinical lead at Treated.

It has been revealed that “Notably, these symptoms are also present in many different conditions, and their presence does not necessarily mean iron deficiency anemia or even low ferritin levels. Similar features are seen in people with iron processing and absorption issues, such as gluten intolerance, or in urgent sudden blood loss scenarios,” added Jonathan Jennings, MD, board certified internist at Medical Offices of Manhattan.

Recent findings suggest that iron deficiency can affect your skin and appearance. These signs are often subtle, but may include:.

According to recent reports, in some ways, the social media videos are correct. Your skin and face can change when your iron levels are low.

Sources indicate that “The facial signs people point to, like pale skin and a washed-out look, mostly come from anaemia, when your haemoglobin has dropped. But iron deficiency and anaemia aren’t the same thing,” said Thom Phillips, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and Chief Medical Officer at Forth. “By the time low iron reveals on your face, your stores are usually close to empty.”.

It is crucial to speak with a healthcare professional, who will run blood tests such as a complete blood count and ferritin levels.

It is also crucial not to take iron supplements without first checking with your healthcare professional, because having too much iron in your body can also cause negative effects.

Too little and too much iron could raise your risk of infection, which is why it’s important not to take supplements without medical supervision.

It has been revealed that the signs and symptoms of iron deficiency can depend on whether you are anemic or not. Some of the early signs may include:.

“These symptoms typically occur because your body produces fewer red blood cells, which results in less oxygen being delivered throughout your body, making you feel tired and weak,” stated Atkinson.

Less common symptoms may include:.

While your facial appearance can be a sign that something isn’t right, healthcare professionals consider other symptoms and how you feel overall.

They also rely on blood tests to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

“The misinformation is the idea that you can spot it yourself. That leads to two problems: people with low iron who look fine assume they’re OK, and people who look tired start taking iron supplements they don’t need,” said Phillips.

Atkinson also noted that factors such as different settings and environmental conditions can affect how your face appears.

That being said, the “ferritin face” trend may help bring awareness to certain symptoms and when to get them checked.

“[This] trend may raise some awareness about iron deficiency anemia and how low iron levels can impact daily life,” stated Atkinson.

Recent findings suggest that “Fatigue and lightheadedness are common side effects of low iron, but it manifests in other ways too, such as paler skin or increased hair shedding, which can be concerning for many people. If you experience these symptoms, you should let your doctor know so they can help treat the condition appropriately,” he noted.

New electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • Created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s users were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

Created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team claims that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

In a recent development, the shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

Researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

The potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

According to recent reports, scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

In a recent development, finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

Those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team indicates more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

It’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

#121276. Latest Update: The Unintended Consequences of Good Intentions

Latest Update: The Unintended Consequences of Good Intentions

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I was intrigued to read a recent article about honeybees aggressively bumping bumblebees out of the way when they alit on the same flowers, mercilessly chasing them off.1.
  • It is a story of unintended consequences.
  • Someone, often a politician, presents what seems a commonsense or creative idea to better a bad situation, then someone else calmly points out all the downsides that just haven’t been thought of.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

I was intrigued to read a recent article about honeybees aggressively bumping bumblebees out of the way when they alit on the same flowers, mercilessly chasing them off.1.

It is a story of unintended consequences. Apparently, the number of registered beekeepers more than doubled between 2010 and 2025, following campaigns encouraging us to get involved in saving endangered insects. Now it seems that this growth in honeybees is having harmful, unforeseen effects on other wild pollinators.1.

It happens so often, doesn’t it? Someone, often a politician, presents what seems a commonsense or creative idea to better a bad situation, then someone else calmly points out all the downsides that just haven’t been thought of.

We are so focused on whatever has our attention that we don’t see the massive picture, leaving us in tunnel vision.

It is something that human givens therapists stay alert to at all times. When our clients focus on a particular view or sense of understanding, we can stay neutral, stand back, and bring attention to elements that they cannot see.

Industry observers note that for instance, a client once consulted me about her blueprint to write a will leaving her worldly goods to just two of her three adult children. She loved them all equally and, on the face of it, her plan seemed logical. Her elder daughter had a lucrative job in finance while her younger daughter was a struggling actor and her son a struggling musician. I pointed out that while her plan made monetary sense, she wasn’t taking into account the potential emotional meaning of leaving money in a will.

Screenwriter, TV producer and novelist Daisy Goodwin has written about this. With her highly successful TV career, she had no financial worries and could accept that her siblings had greater need of the proceeds of their mother’s estate when she died. Her mother left Daisy just a small cash sum and some personal items and wrote in her will, “I leave my daughter Daisy out of the estate not because I love her any less but because I think she has less need of it.”.

Sources indicate that daisy’s response? “But, and here’s the rub, although I know in my head that my mother’s will is fair, in my heart I feel left out. I love my siblings dearly, and I don’t begrudge them the money; I can understand they need it more than I do, but all the same I feel rejected. I am pretty sure that this was not my mother’s intention; she was trying to do the right thing as she saw it, but the result left me, a decade later, still trying to fight the feeling that she left me out of her will because she loved me less.”2.

It is a good example of seeing just part of the picture and thinking others will view things as we do. Often, in such cases, what is conceived in generosity ends up causing unforeseen rifts in the family.

Michael was devastated when a presentation he had spent his personal time on was rejected without explanation. He had had “a revolutionary idea” that, he believed, would reposition the organization in a way that would drive a host of fresh clients to them. He expected his bosses to be as excited as he was and arranged a meeting with the chief executive officer and second-in-command to demonstrate his vision in a dramatic video, packed with punch.

To his astonishment, his presentation was met with silence. Then he was politely thanked and told that “they would think about it.” Eventually, he received an email saying the company would not be pursuing his idea.

Industry observers note that what Michael had entirely ignored in his single-minded focus on his vision were perspectives other than his own. His bosses felt undermined, and that the current approach, which they had masterminded, was being disrespected. Instead of taking into account their need for a sense of status and achievement, he had ridden roughshod over their ideas, expecting them to receive this gladly. The irony is that they probably all lost out. It was a honeybee manoeuvre, with no good outcome for anyone, when, correctly thought through and introduced gradually, outcomes might have been very different.

Industry observers note that when we want to bring about change, we may have only the best of intentions. But we have to bring others with us, including critics or those who may be affected in ways that they don’t initially like. Putting ourselves in others’ shoes and foreseeing unwanted outcomes remain the unmissable first steps in all such circumstances.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that NETFLIX’S LATEST HEADLINE-MAKING limited series The Altruists has a lot of major names attached to it.
  • Well, if you’ve avoided the cryptocurrency market and carbon-positive NFT gorillas in the past several years, we can’t really blame you.
  • Why is this story about fraud (of which Bankman-Fried was eventually convicted) called The Altruists?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that NETFLIX’S LATEST HEADLINE-MAKING limited series The Altruists has a lot of major names attached to it. There are Irish and American actors Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner, respectively, playing up their dorkiest selves to portray Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison. (Ostensibly while Garner desperately awaits casting in a possible Madonna biopic that has been in development hell for what feels like forever.).

Who, you ask? Well, if you’ve avoided the cryptocurrency market and carbon-positive NFT gorillas in the past several years, we can’t really blame you. But what you need to know is that Bankman-Fried and Ellison were the heads of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX as well as lovers. FTX, and the love between them, notoriously collapsed when Bankman-Fried was arrested and accused of stealing over $8 billion in customer funds.

Why is this story about fraud (of which Bankman-Fried was eventually convicted) called The Altruists? Ironically, FTX was purportedly created as a firm that gave away as much as it earned, based on the principle of effective altruism—words that got everyone in the finance world hot and heavy with excitement. Until news came out that Bankman-Fried and other FTX executives had spent billion-dollar-sized wads of cash “on luxury hotel stays, private planes, DoorDash orders, trips to Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville, and, in the case of one top executive, a $2.5 million yacht,” Business Insider reports. FTX was also known for hosting an ultra-luxe conference in the Bahamas that featured famous folks including Bill Clinton, Tom Brady, and the musicians Steve Aoki and the late Liam Payne of One Direction, who in 2024 fell to his death from a hotel balcony in Argentina at the age of 31.

In a recent development, so, yeah, we’re dealing with a twisted and extremely millennial story full of curveballs and screwballs. But whether you’re watching The Altruists or simply hearing about it, what do you need to know about the true FTX story at the heart of it? We’ve got you covered below.

The Altruists is as much a love story as it is a story of financial doom: The two were intertwined with Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, who met at an investment firm and fell in love. Bankman-Fried would found FTX as well as its sister cryptocurrency trading firm Alameda Research, while Ellison was CEO of Alameda Research, which funneled money from FTX.

In a recent development, FTX was on an upward trajectory in the early 2020s, garnering Bankman-Fried the nickname of “Crypto King.” The company, once worth $32 billion, nosedived into bankruptcy in 2022 while also being investigated by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Justice Department. Bankman-Fried “sounded surprisingly calm” in an interview with The New York Times amid FTX’s freefall. “You would’ve thought that I’d be getting no sleep right now, and instead I’m getting some,” he told the publication. “It could be worse.”.

Yes. In fact, things could and did get a lot worse for this once seemingly altruistic finance dude. He and Ellison broke off their romantic relationship amid FTX’s collapse in 2022. (“She wanted more from it than I was able to give,” Bankman-Fried testified, according to the Wall Street Journal. To which one can only wonder: More than $8 billion?).

On March 28, 2024, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and was additionally ordered to “pay $11 billion in forfeiture for his orchestration of multiple fraudulent schemes,” the Justice Department confirmed.

In total, he was convicted of two counts of wire fraud, two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Sources indicate that what’s curious is that his right-hand woman, Ellison, only got less than two years in prison for her part in the cryptocurrency fraud, though she did plead guilty to two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, two counts of wire fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit commodities fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. She was also ordered to forfeit $11 billion.

Her relatively light sentence can be explained by the fact that, though the “very math-y” Stanford graduate helped orchestrate the multibillion-dollar scheme alongside Bankman-Fried, she became a star witness for the prosecution against her former boyfriend. The prosecutors offered her a sweetened deal to shorten her prison time in exchange for cooperation, information, and testimony.

She testified, NPR reports, that as Alameda found itself in a financial hole, Bankman-Fried directed her to take more money from FTX customers to bail the tech giant out. “We were in a bad situation,” she said.

U.S. Attorney Damian Williams mentioned of Bankman-Fried’s scheme that it was “one of the largest financial frauds in history, stealing over $8 billion of his customers’ money.”.

Their love may be over, and they are both convicted felons, all of which gets packed into the final episode of the eight-part The Altruists. But at least Ellison is moving on. Sort of. After being imprisoned for less than two years, she is now a free woman.

In September, Ellison formally joined Manifund “to develop our funding platform and research how to effectively direct philanthropic dollars,” the company’s CEO Austin Chen announced, per Oxygen. She had reportedly joined the nonprofit funding platform and philanthropic organization on a trial basis at first and went by the innocent-sounding pseudonym “Carol.” This work is in line with her stated belief in effective altruism, which in turn became a multibillion-dollar con, which doesn’t sound all that altruistic or effective.

Sources indicate that “On FTX itself, I remain conflicted. It was their money and spirit that enabled the Future Fund, and I still admire many aspects of FTX and the individuals who worked there,” Chen wrote. “But also: FTX did wrong. Its collapse harmed users (myself included), and damaged the movement which I deeply care about.”.

Chen is a big believer in redemption. “I’d like to give her the opportunity to contribute back to the world,” he wrote. “I hope that the world will concur.” Which is very generous of him. Maybe she’ll even get a Nathan Fielder-hosted documentary one day.

Industry observers note that bankman-Fried, meanwhile? He’s still behind bars on that 25-year sentence. Thankfully for him, however, he is incarcerated at the low-security California federal prison Federal Correctional Institution Lompoc, which is known for its open dormitory and room-type housing.

Maybe he will find a newly introduced way to be altruistic. Or, at least, stop committing federal crimes.

The FIA began the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend by announcing that all manufacturers have agreed to the framework to bring turbocharged V8 engines back to F1 and move away from the current V6 turbo.

This move has long been expected, with hopes that it will make engine building easier and cheaper while bringing back the sound that motorsport fans deeply miss.

The sound of the V8 engines was a rally cry for fans and has been sorely missed by audiences worldwide.

The F1 engine manufacturers agreed to a rough-out overarching strategy to move to a 2.1-liter turbocharged V8 from 2030 onwards, with a lower charge of electrical power reducing the hybrid output from 350kW to 200kW, a decrease of nearly 56 percent.

The FIA declared that ‘The proposal is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing.”.

With everyone in agreement, PU manufacturers will start to jockey between improving the upcoming car entering a sophomore season of new regulations and game planning for the major change coming just three seasons down the line.

It’s been 13 years since manufacturers last built a V8 engine for F1.

“This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1,” FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem stated. “From the outset, I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.

Recent findings suggest that “The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this Championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition.”.

A separate power cabinet can send up to 1 MW across as many as eight vehicles at once, shifting power between them as their charging needs change. Operators can configure it with CCS or NACS plugs for passenger EVs or a Megawatt Charging System (MCS) plug for compatible heavy-duty trucks.

Sources indicate that alpitronic’s 400 kW chargers were already being made in Wisconsin for Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging in 2024. Alpitronic Americas CEO Patrik Herrnegger mentioned the Fort Mill plant “will put US production under our direct control, bring us closer to our customers, and enable us to serve them more efficiently.”.

In a recent development, the 173,315-square-foot site at 3560 Stateview Blvd. (pictured above) will also house a testing lab, repair operations, a warehouse, logistics space, and offices. South Carolina approved job development credits and awarded York County a $200,000 grant to help pay for building improvements.

Alpitronic expects to start operations in February 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

Industry observers note that “We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike noted in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

In a recent development, last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that demonstrated intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a upcoming approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

“Fiona was such a gift,” said Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

  • Industry observers note that it’s notable to get this out of the way now: Cooling sheets aren’t magic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that I always thought cooling sheets were a marketing gimmick until I actually tried them while I was nine months pregnant—in the middle of July. It was the first time in months that I didn’t wake up with my sweaty hair matted against my head, and I’ve never looked back.

Industry observers note that it’s notable to get this out of the way now: Cooling sheets aren’t magic. They’re not going to keep you from sweating if you sleep under a heavy comforter or it’s warm in your bedroom at night. But they do cause a noticeable difference in how you feel between the sheets, and are one more element to help regulate your body temperature at night.

These are a few of our favorite sheet sets, but read on for more detailed reviews:.

It has been revealed that “The ideal temperature for sleeping is no cooler than 66 degrees and no warmer than 72 degrees,” says neuroscientist and sleep specialist Allison Brager, PhD. “This was study-approved, tested, and evaluated by some NASA scientists.” Resting in this temperate climate can support better sleep and, ultimately, improved health. Regularly shortchanging your sleep leads to a higher risk of obesity, depression, and type 2 diabetes, along with other health issues. But having good, consistent sleep can do the opposite.

That’s why, even though cooling sheets are usually more expensive than regular sheets, they’re a worthwhile investment that will help support more restorative sleep, Brager says, and, as a result, improve your overall quality of life.

So, how can you tell which bedding option will help you hit that not-so-hot spot? Cooling sheets—especially those made from fabrics like microfiber, linen, and bamboo—can help keep your body at the right temp for restful sleep. The best cooling sheets can help reduce heat buildup and manage moisture, but your comfort also depends on your room and bedding.

The Regulator sheets are made from rayon derived from bamboo and felt lightweight, silky, and cool to the touch, according to our testers.

“They’re very soft, and I’m able to wake up not sweaty,” indicates Women’s Health digital designer Taryn Colbert, who has zero complaints about these sheets.

WH contributor and self-professed "hot sleeper" Lily Wohlner is also a fan. She had never owned a set of cooling sheets, but promptly fell in love with these. They're "super thin, which automatically makes them nice and light,” Wohlner indicates. “But they're also temperature-regulating and moisture-wicking, so you stay fresh and cool while you snooze.” She also loves how silky smooth they feel against the skin without that "crunchy" feeling found in lesser, lower-quality sheets.

In a recent development, there is one catch to the ultra-lightweight design, however. "Due to their weight, I find that these sheets tend to bunch up at the bottom of my bed, which I don't love," Wohlner says. "Every time I go to make my bed, I have to fish under my comforter to find them, which adds time to the already dreaded process." (Colbert hasn’t experienced this.).

It has been revealed that it's not a deal-breaker for us, but something to be aware of. Plus, we found that the natural stretch of these sheets means making (or re-making) the bed is a snap.

Bamboo is often touted as more eco-friendly because it's possible to harvest more per acre than cotton and is typically grown without pesticides. However, the experts we spoke with warned that the raw material goes through serious chemical refinement before it's turned into bedding.

Sources indicate that overall, our team loved these sheets for their buttery soft, featherweight design and the ability to keep us cool and sweat-free even on the hottest summer nights. They're a great midrange set that we recommend for anyone looking to level up from the cheapest available options (like Mellanni's four-piece Iconic Sheet Set), but who isn't quite ready to splurge on an ultra-luxe set.

Read more: Best Weighted Blankets.

According to recent reports, “Jill of all trades; master of none.” That's the perfect way to describe Mellanni's Iconic Collection, including the four-piece set of cooling sheets we tested for this year's roundup. These sheets aren't the softest, the most luxurious, or the absolute best at cooling. But they are a solid all-around buy that feels better, looks better, and cools better than most other sets that cost three times as much.

"My girlfriend and I have slept on these for the last month, and we've been pleasantly surprised by how good they feel for the price," Richard notes. "They feel much better and cozier against the skin than most other sheets I've tested in this price range.".

According to recent reports, fellow tester and self-described hot sleeper Janie Booth, associate video producer at WH, also praises the feel of these sheets. “They are very soft,” she notes.

It has been revealed that the synthetic microfiber construction in this sheet set isn't purposely designed for cooling. In fact, the weave is tighter than other sheets made with natural fibers. But the material is thin enough to be surprisingly breathable, without feeling threadbare. "I actually took these glamping on a long, hot, late June weekend," Richard says. "For sticky, sweaty nights, the thickness of these sheets was perfect, and I found them much more breathable than most microfiber sheets.".

Sources indicate that on the downside, that same microfiber—polyester, really—construction means these aren't as absorbent or moisture-wicking as natural alternatives either. So, they're not as good at whisking away sweat to help further cool your body.

According to recent reports, like most microfiber fabrics, these sheets are surprisingly durable, though, thanks to the previously mentioned tight weave. We've found they hold up well, even after repeated washings with no loose threads, shedding, or fading. (Booth noticed some pilling, but Richard didn’t.) Plus, they're more wrinkle-resistant than most.

Industry observers note that the biggest thing these cooling sheets have going for them is price. They're significantly cheaper (in some cases, by more than 75 percent) than every other set in this year's roundup. Plus, with Amazon's generous free shipping and free returns policy, it's almost like you're getting a legit in-home sleep trial.

One additional bonus is that these sheets are available in a much wider selection of colors and patterns than any other we tested. That's especially nice if you're keen to match the look of your new cooling sheets to the rest of your bedroom decor.

Read more: Best Cooling Mattresses.

It has been revealed that there are a lot of high-tech fabric blends out there designed to keep you cool, but classic cotton sheets can still work wonders. Brooklinen’s Classic Percale Core Sheet Set is a favorite in my household—so much so that I’ll try to wash them swiftly when I do laundry to get them back on my mattress before I need to swap in a different set. These were the sheets I splurged on when I was heavily pregnant and hot. They still feel luxurious and crisp, even though I’ve had them in heavy rotation for two years.

It has been revealed that the sheets are made with percale cotton, which means it’s woven into a grid pattern to give it a crisp, cool feel. It’s almost like a dress shirt, but softer, and with a noticeable coolness when you slide between the sheets.

Christian Gollayan, style and reviews director at Men's Health and Women's Health, is also a fan. “I’m a hot sleeper and usually need my bedroom below 69 degrees to avoid getting sweaty,” he indicates. “These kept me comfortable through fall, winter, and spring.”.

In a recent development, gollayan says his sheets held up “remarkably well” for nearly two years with weekly washings. When he did sweat in deep summer, Gollayan says his sheets didn’t hold onto an odor the way some other sets he’s tried have. The sheets have thoughtful details that I love, too, like envelope closures to keep your pillows from sliding out and tags that designate which end of the fitted sheet is the long and short side.

While Gollayan and I both enjoy these sheets, he noticed some fraying in his set after two years. (I haven’t had the same experience, although the rich blue color in my tandem stripes is fading.) They also felt a little stiff at first, but swiftly soften up with time and repeat washings. They’re not the cheapest cooling sheets you’ll find, but they’re pretty durable and luxe.

According to recent reports, casper is perhaps best known for its excellent cooling mattresses. But you might be surprised to learn the company also makes great cooling bedding. After testing over a dozen cooling sheets, Casper's Hyperlite Sheet Set earned our 'Best Runner-Up' spot for its soft, ultra-lightweight feel, the fact it looks more premium than its price should allow, and, most importantly, its 100 percent Tencel Lyocell construction. The fabric excels at fighting sweat and overheating, thanks to its structure, which absorbs and releases moisture while promoting good airflow.

“They're definitely cooling without being too ‘cold,’” claims WH digital designer and tester Leeann Mattern. Fellow tester Mike Richard also praises the sheets’ lightweight, cooling feel, which he says is great year-round. But, in warmer weather, he says they do an excellent job at regulating temperature and wicking away sweat and moisture. That's thanks in large part to the tencel lyocell material and the unique, vented grid-weave pattern that Casper uses to help promote better airflow while you sleep. Bonus: Our team loved that same grid pattern elevates the vibe of these sheets above the traditional (and often boring) flat aesthetic of most sheets with a lightly textured look and feel.

We're hard-pressed to find much to complain about with these cooling sheets, but there are a few minor concerns to keep in mind. "My only gripe is that I wish they were a little softer because they're not quite as buttery or luxurious as the true bamboo and bamboo blend options we tested," Richard says. That's largely due to their lower 200-thread-count construction (incidentally, that was the lowest of any sheets we tested this year). "I did find that they soften after a few washes, however, and hold up well to repeated machine-washings, too.".

Mattern also indicates the lightweight fabric allows patterns in her mattress and pillow to show through, so that’s something to be aware of if you’re especially concerned about aesthetics. On that note, our team of sleep testers were a bit bummed by the lack of available color options—this sheet set only comes in white.

According to recent reports, we would also love it if Casper expanded its return policy beyond the lackluster 30 days. That's surprisingly thin compared to the competition, and the sheets must be returned in their original, unused condition, which doesn't allow for a true "sleep trial.".

Read more: Best Cooling Mattress Toppers.

Industry observers note that of course, you don't have to spend hundreds to score a decent set of cooling sheets. But, sometimes, you really do get what you pay for. That's true of Bedgear's Ver-Tex Sheet Set. They're pricier than most we tested this year, but oh so worth it with a performance-minded design that keeps you cool and stays put, even during your most "vigorous" bed activities.

The Ver-Tex Sheet Set is the only one in this year's roundup made of 100 percent nylon. Like many synthetic materials, nylon isn't typically absorbent or very good at wicking away moisture. "I initially planned to test these out in my guest room," Richard says. "But my girlfriend and I loved how cool-to-the-touch they were, and found them way softer and airier than we expected, so we wound up putting them on our bed.".

In a recent development, the nylon is extremely breathable, allowing them to cool better than most. In very humid environments (think Miami in August), however, we did notice that they felt slightly clammier than other natural fabric sets our team tested. “This is such a ridiculous thing to say, but they almost did their job too well,” claims fellow tester and WH social media editor Alyssa Cruz. “I sometimes wake up cold and need to add extra blankets.” Because of this, she aims to switch them out during the chillier winter months.

According to recent reports, still, our team agrees that these sheets are worth the $300 price tag. “I love the feeling the most,” Cruz states. “These are the softest sheets I have ever felt, and almost feel like activewear. They make falling asleep feel luxurious.”.

Industry observers note that plus, one of this set's biggest selling points is its ability to stretch and provide an extremely good fit, thanks to Bedgear's unique Powerband. It's a thick, full-band elastic designed to grip the bottom of your mattress so it won't slip. The pillowcases included with the Ver-Tex sets also feature this same band, so we never wound up with our pillows inching their way out of the case. Everything stays put, so you're not left remaking the bed every night before tucking in.

There's almost nothing we dislike about these best-in-class cooling sheets. But we do wish they were available in more than four colors. They're also not sold in smaller sizes like Twin, Twin XL, or Full, which may or may not be a deal-breaker for you.

In a recent development, lastly, these are among the priciest cooling sheets we tested over the past year. Still, we think you get what you pay for with this set. They're extremely durable, cool better than almost every other set we tested, and the ultra-snug fit for both the sheets and pillowcases is second to none.

Recent findings suggest that peachSkinSheets’ Classic Collection has a brushed polyester fabric that our testers found super soft. Somehow PeachSkinSheets manages to thread that needle (pun intended) with its Classic Collection. With an airy, breathable, smart poly-fiber construction, these sheets are surprisingly effective at keeping you cool, calm, and collected.

"I tested these in our guest suite, and the in-laws (self-described 'fussy' sleepers) and I both agreed that these do an incredible job at keeping you cool during the night," Richard indicates. "They feel more premium, more luxurious than the price tag would suggest." But more importantly, our entire test staff found these kept us cool while also doing a reasonable job of managing sweat and moisture. The athletic-grade construction is lighter than traditional cotton, and they breathe more like high-end (think Lululemon) athleisure apparel.

The sheets are OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certified, meaning they have been tested against limits for harmful substances. "My girlfriend has extremely sensitive skin, and even basic synthetics like polyester don't always agree with her, sometimes causing rashes and irritation," Richard says. "We were initially skeptical about these poly-fiber sheets, but she's had zero issues and finds them extremely comfortable.".

The feel of these sheets was also a perk for WH associate style and reviews editor Shannen Zitz. “The sheets are super soft and smooth without causing me to overheat at night,” she notes.

According to recent reports, zitz praises the deep corners of the fitted sheet, too. “I love that the fitted sheet actually stays on my bed,” she indicates. “My biggest problem with sheets is when they slip off the corners after just a few nights, but these have really deep corners so they stay put really well.” Every set also includes an extender panel, allowing the sheets to fit extra-deep (up to 22-inch) mattresses which covers just about every model on the market.

Unlike most of the competition, they're available in more than 30 colorways—everything from basic white and navy to bolder options like gold and neon orange—making it easy to match the aesthetic of your current bedroom setup.

Sources indicate that after several months of testing, we found the Classic Collection cooling sheets to be extremely durable. "Even after repeated machine-washing and with two cats in my house, these sheets have stood up to teeth, claws, pills, pulls, and fading," Richard indicates. "Plus, fresh out of the wash, the wrinkles release almost instantly after making the bed, so I never have to worry about ironing them." The only gripe, per Zitz, is that the top sheet felt a little short. “I toss and turn a lot and, after a night or two, I find the bottom of the sheet comes untucked pretty easily,” she says. “If you like your sheets to feel really snug, it requires re-tucking.”.

Recent findings suggest that peachSkinSheets also shines with a solid, 30-day return policy. Like SlumberCloud, it's more like an in-home sleep trial. Even opened bedding can be returned within 30 days for a full refund, so it's truly risk-free to try them out at home.

It has been revealed that most cooling bedding products are designed to draw away and evaporate moisture. But that means they only start working after you're already sweating and are probably miserable. Slumber Cloud's Performance Sheets take a different tack with a uniquely blended construction that actively regulates temperature the entire time you're sleeping to (ideally) keep you cool and comfortable before sweat ever becomes an problem.

Industry observers note that the secret sauce to Slumber Cloud's Performance Sheets is a blend of reactive Tencel with Outlast viscose. Tencel is already one of our favorite fibers for cooling sheets, but the addition of Outlast levels up the entire setup. "I've used Outlast-infused hiking apparel before, and it's incredibly effective at regulating body temperature in hot or cold environments," Richard says. "The addition of Outlast in these sheets delivers best-in-class moisture-wicking, which is a game-changer if you're a hot (and potentially clammy) sleeper." The 300-thread-count material might appear to be lower quality than higher-end 500-plus-thread-count alternatives. But, these feel every bit softer than many premium sheets we've previously tested.

According to recent reports, these sheets are soft to the touch, according to fellow tester and WH entertainment editor Amy Wilkinson. “But my absolute favorite thing about these sheets, which I've never encountered with another set, is the additional elastic band at the corners of the fitted sheet that help it wrap around virtually any size mattress you can imagine,” she states. Compared to the traditional "corner-sewn" elastics found in most traditional fitted sheets, the bands in this sheet set help keep it firmly in place.

One especially nice feature of all of Slumber Cloud's bedding: it offers a 30-night trial for purchases made directly from the brand.

If you’re an extra-hot sleeper, however, you may want to look elsewhere. While Wilkinson found these sheets cooling, she says that, despite claims about being designed with “NASA cooling technology,” they didn’t seem to cool her off better than her previous sheet set. Still, they are great at wicking moisture and are incredibly durable.

(Pro tip: The Performance Sheet Set is, in our opinion, Slumber Cloud's best cooling sheet set. But, if you're looking for almost-as-good performance with a classic sheet feel, opt for its Essential Sheet Set which blends cotton with Outlast fibers.).

If you love the silky smoothness of cotton sateen sheets, Sijo’s AiryWeight Eucalyptus Sheets offer a similar feel while being 70 percent more moisture-absorbing. Made with naturally hypoallergenic Tencel Lyocell, the glossy silk-like texture of the sheets is a great option for those with sensitive skin, especially if certain materials make you feel itchy. Plus, the set boasts OEKO-TEX and Asthma and Allergy Friendly certifications.

“The feel of these are incredible,” indicates WH fitness editor Cori Ritchey. “With cooling sheets, I tend to fear they're going to be too slick and not cozy. These are kind of the perfect blend.” The sheets feel silky but not slippery, she adds.

In a recent development, at $185 for a queen-size set, these Sijo sheets aren’t cheap, but they are long lasting. The brand claims the sheets survived 2,000 rubs without pilling in lab testing. They passed Ritchey’s personal durability test, too: “They wash very nicely—they don't seem to lose their texture the longer you use them,” she notes. And for those of us whose top sheet ends up on the floor most nights, you can subtract the flat sheet from the set for a $75 discount.

One of the downsides of the sheets is the two-month return window that only applies if the bedding is unopened—but there is a catch here. Sijo offers a 30-night bedding trial for eligible direct purchases. Return-shipping charges depend on whether you purchased Checkout+, so check the terms before ordering. Some customers have also noted that the sheets shrink a little after the first wash (we didn’t notice this during testing, but it’s worth flagging).

Some hot sleepers merely need sheets that are breathable throughout the night, while others prefer bedding that is immediately cool to the touch. If you want a set of sheets that feels like sleeping on the cool side of the pillow all night long, Sijo’s AiryWeight Eucalyptus Sheets are for you. “I'm normally a hot sleeper and these have kept me cool and comfortable,” Ritchey says.

It has been revealed that linen sheets are a great option for hot sleepers, if you’re willing to spend a little more. Brooklinen’s Linen Core Sheets are made with 100 percent European flax that softens with each wash, although they may be a little rough for sensitive skin right out of the box. The sheets are breathable yet they have a weight to them, which makes them great for year-round use.

Recent findings suggest that “These sheets are so soft and cozy—truly the most comfortable material I have ever slept on,” says WH associate editor Olivia Luppino. “I actively look forward to getting into bed with them.” She describes the sheets as plush to the touch, while still maintaining a sleekness that gives them a cooling feel. “They definitely keep me cool in warm summer months,” she says. “I’m very into these sheets.”.

That remarked, one of the (few) downsides is the $300-plus price tag, which is expensive but not outrageous when it comes to linen sheets. Plus, Brooklinen tends to run frequent sales, so it’s not unusual to see a 25 percent discount. The sheets have gotten softer with each wash, but at the same time they wear like iron with no snagging, pulling, or pilling to be found.

According to recent reports, they are also OEKO-TEX certified and come with the longest return window of our favorite cooling sheets at a whopping 365 days. If you’re looking to make an investment that will last and keep you cool in any climate, Brooklinen’s Linen Core Sheets are worth the splurge.

Industry observers note that to curate a list of the best cooling sheets, we recruited eight Women's Health staffers to personally vet a wide range of sets in various temperatures and environments over the past year. For instance, we slept in Casper's Hyperlite Sheet Set in July with no air-conditioning, glamped with Mellanni's Iconic Collection in New Hampshire, and cozied up in SlumberCloud's Performance Sheet Set with the window open in 80-degree heat “for science.” Then, our testing editors narrowed the selections by evaluating each sheet set based on style, fit, price point, comfort, breathability, moisture management, softness, durability after washing, wrinkling or pilling, and value.

It probably goes without saying that sheet material matters above all else. Natural fibers, like linen and cotton, are often best, according to Brager. They tend to be more breathable and absorbent (more on why that's actually a good thing below) than others, which means they won't trap heat that can make you sweat as you catch your Z's.

Recent findings suggest that your sheets’ weave is the pattern used to hold the threads together to make the fabric. Percale is generally considered the best weave for hot sleepers. This type of weave uses a simple pattern that maximizes airflow and has a lightweight feel, lowering the odds it will trap body heat while you snooze.

Sources indicate that it’s generally recommended that you avoid sateen or flannel sheets if you’re looking for a cooling feel. These tend to be denser and hold onto heat as a result.

There are so many factors that go into how cool you feel when you slip between the sheets at night, including the temperature of your room, your body temperature, the weight of your comforter, and your mattress composition. But we sweat a lot throughout the night. "If you don't have something that's absorbent, you will marinate in sweat," Young indicates. That's why natural materials that are highly absorbent, like linen and cotton, are vital. "Even more important than that is wicking, which means getting moisture to the surface for evaporation," says Young. The two of these features working in tandem is what keeps you both dry and cool.

Sources indicate that moisture-wicking sheets can be one element to help keep you cool at night. These sheets are specially designed to pull moisture away from your skin and evaporate, allowing you to feel cooler, faster. They also tend to feel a little airier than other sheets.

That doesn’t mean you won’t ever feel hot if you use moisture-wicking sheets—again, there’s a lot happening when you sleep that can influence your body’s temperature. But you can usually feel a difference between how you feel when using moisture-wicking sheets and other types of sheets.

Sources indicate that beyond the material of your cooling sheets, the quality of that material is important. Back in the day, thread count was the single most important measure of quality in bedding. Anything above 600-thread-count was often considered good, while 800 and above was downright luxurious. But advances in technology have allowed us to create sheets with a 1,500, even 2,000, thread count. That’s not necessarily a good thing, as that figure can be inflated and used as a marketing gimmick.

Plus, super-high thread-count sheets usually aren’t all they're cracked up to be. “My experience with those is that they’re not strong, and they don’t hold up well,” notes Deborah Young, owner of TheTextileExpert.com and a clinical assistant professor of textiles at Arizona State University. “They are seductively soft, but for me, there’s a point of diminishing returns.”.

Recent findings suggest that thread count can be a measure of quality, but you'll want to consider other factors, too, especially when shopping for the best cooling sheets. Some manufacturers rely on GSM (or grams per square meter) as this is a measure of weight rather than thread density.

Industry observers note that young's most notable tip for hot sleepers, however, is that they may actually benefit from sheets with a lower thread count (like 400). A higher thread count often means the sheets are denser, offering better coverage, but a hot sleeper would probably want to avoid this.

It depends. Every brand we recommend below offers a return policy with a minimum 30-day term. Some, however, only accept returns for unopened sheet sets in the original packaging. Others provide longer terms (up to 365 days) with no questions asked, effectively like a free in-home trial.

Industry observers note that there are a variety of certifications out there to ensure that consumers are getting high-quality bedding and textiles. One of the most common labels you’ll find on sheets is the OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification, which means that the product has been tested for more than 1,000 harmful substances. Some sheets may also have sustainability labels, like FSC certification, or an Asthma & Allergy Friendly certification from the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. Keep in mind that more certifications tend to lead to a higher price tag, though—and not all are necessary.

Our favorite cooling sheets range in price from $37 to $322 for a queen-size set. There’s no need to spend hundreds on a set of sheets—you can easily find high-quality cooling sheets for $100-plus. However, certain fabrics like linen will cost more and in return should survive many years of use.

It has been revealed that women’s Health first wrote this story in 2019 and has been continuously testing new cooling sheets as they’re released. During that time, some clear favorites have emerged. For this update, we had several WH staffers and contributors test these products in their own beds. Each sheet set was tested for two to three weeks or longer, and evaluated on their cooling abilities, softness, and durability, among other factors. Testers ranged from those who regularly wake up sweaty to people who consider themselves “neutral” in terms of sleep temperature.

It has been revealed that yes, cooling sheets actually work. They’re designed to be lightweight, breathable, and moisture-wicking, all of which can make you feel cooler when you sleep at night. However, there are a lot of factors that influence how hot you feel at night, including the type of mattress and comforter you have. Ultimately, cooling sheets are one more way to help you feel comfortable, but they shouldn’t be the only thing you use if you tend to run hot while you sleep.

Cotton is usually considered best, but you have a few options to choose from when it comes to cooling materials for sheets.

Bamboo sheets can be cooler than cotton sheets, but that’s not always the case. The weave of your sheets matters. A cotton percale weave sheet can be very cooling and even more cooling than standard bamboo sheets. But cotton is also used to make flannel sheets—which are heat-insulating, not cooling—making it hard to rely on fabric alone when choosing the best cooling sheets.

Recent findings suggest that thread count is usually linked to the softness of sheets, but it can impact how cool sheets feel. A higher thread count typically means that sheets are denser, which can work against your efforts to stay cool. That’s why Young suggests choosing sheets with a lower thread count, like 400, over much higher thread count options.

Sources indicate that cooling sheets should be washed as often as “regular” sheets, which means they should be washed every week, notes Kelly Murray, a certified pediatric and adult sleep coach in Chicago. This will allow you to wash away any allergens, keeping your sheets feeling crisp and fresh, she adds.

According to recent reports, by the way, you should wash your cooling sheets before using them, too. "You're washing off any dust the sheets may have collected in the warehouse, which can irritate your respiratory system and lead to sleep issues,” Murray says.

In a recent development, some cooling sheets, especially those made with natural fibers like cotton and linen, soften with each successive wash. If your upcoming set feels a little too stiff or "crunchy," try running them through a machine wash cycle or two to soften them.

Recent findings suggest that there is an almost universal rule among experts that you should be changing your sheets every week, and Murray concurs. If you don't want to wash your sheets that often, you should consider purchasing an extra set to swap out each week.

Industry observers note that as for when it's time to swap out cooling sheets for brand latest ones, that's up to you. Murray says she purchases a new set whenever she sees them on sale, but recommends replacing yours about every two to three years.

Industry observers note that ICYDK, your body temperature needs to drop about 2 degrees lower at night in order to synthesize melatonin, Murray says. So, it is super crucial that you create an environment that allows for this. That means ensuring your bedroom is "dark, cool, and quiet" when you're ready for bed.

In a recent development, other than investing in some cooling sheets, you can also improve your sleep quality by keeping a consistent sleep routine that involves ending screen time at least an hour before you go to bed. "Your body and brain are always looking for patterns throughout the day to know what happens next," Murray indicates. "So if you have a consistent bedtime routine that's very relaxing, that will trigger the production of melatonin and help your brain to unwind.".

When Saying ‘No’ to an Aging Parent Is Complicated

💡 Key Takeaways
